articles.title: A Quick Guide to Go's Assembler
articles.summary: The Go compiler uses a unique form of assembly language, based on the input style of the Plan 9 assemblers, which is documented in detail elsewhere. The assembler is not a direct representation of the underlying machine, but rather a semi-abstract instruction set that the compiler operates on. This means that some machine-specific operations appear as themselves, while more general concepts like memory move and subroutine call and return are more abstract. The assembler program is used to parse a description of the semi-abstract instruction set and turn it into instructions to be input to the linker.

articles.title: sshole
articles.summary: The first Unix password hash was stored in the /etc/passwd file, with the username and account name, and the password hash was stored in the /etc/shadow file. The password hash was never encrypted, and the password was not checked for validity. This was changed in the 1990s with the introduction of the Unix password hash, which uses a salt to prevent rainbow table attacks. However, the Unix password hash is not secure, and it is vulnerable to attacks such as brute force and dictionary attacks. The Unix password hash is also not checked for validity, which can lead to unauthorized access to the system.
